wallpapers.title: SEAHORSE VALLEY
wallpapers.line1: The gap between the Mandelbrot set's body and head: spirals of seahorse tails, lined with tiny copies of the whole set.
wallpapers.line2: Mandelbrot set at -0.7453 + 0.1127i, about 680× closer than the whole set  ·  colours: Omarchy's Tokyo Night

wallpapers.title: THE MANDELBROT SET
wallpapers.line1: Every point c where z → z² + c, started at 0, never runs off to infinity. The glow shows how fast the others escape.
wallpapers.line2: First drawn by Robert Brooks and Peter Matelski in 1978, made famous by Benoit Mandelbrot in 1980  ·  colours: Catppuccin

wallpapers.title: ELEPHANT VALLEY
wallpapers.line1: Beside the cusp on the right of the Mandelbrot set's main body, the spirals curl like rows of elephant trunks.
wallpapers.line2: Mandelbrot set at 0.2925 + 0.0149i, about 370× closer than the whole set  ·  colours: Everforest

wallpapers.title: DOUADY'S RABBIT
wallpapers.line1: A Julia set: the same rule z → z² + c, but with c fixed and z starting at each point. Three ears meet at every joint.
wallpapers.line2: c = -0.1226 + 0.7449i, named after the French mathematician Adrien Douady  ·  colours: Nord

wallpapers.title: THE BURNING SHIP
wallpapers.line1: A cousin of the Mandelbrot set that makes both parts of z positive before squaring. This is one of its small ships.
wallpapers.line2: Found by Michael Michelitsch and Otto Rössler in 1992, drawn upside down as usual so the ship sails upright  ·  colours: Matte Black

wallpapers.title: NEWTON'S METHOD
wallpapers.line1: Every point slides toward one of the three cube roots of 1. Where it cannot decide, the borders braid without end.
wallpapers.line2: z³ = 1, the question Arthur Cayley raised in 1879; computers first drew the answer a century later  ·  colours: Kanagawa

wallpapers.title: ZIRCON CITY
wallpapers.line1: A Lyapunov fractal: gold where a simple growth rule settles down, blue-green where it turns to chaos.
wallpapers.line2: Sequence BBBBBBAAAAAA, a from 3.4 to 4.0, b from 2.5 to 3.4; Lyapunov fractals by Mario Markus, late 1980s  ·  colours: Gruvbox

wallpapers.title: THE BUDDHABROT
wallpapers.line1: Not where points escape but the paths they take on the way out, stacked up like a long exposure of the night sky.
wallpapers.line2: Found by Melinda Green in 1993; paths under 50, 500 and 5,000 steps in blue, peach and gold  ·  colours: Ethereal

wallpapers.title: THE MANDELBULB
wallpapers.line1: The Mandelbrot idea taken into 3D: the squaring is done with angles in space, to the eighth power.
wallpapers.line2: Found by Daniel White and Paul Nylander in 2009, lit and drawn here from its formula  ·  colours: Ristretto
